Tim Lamb

Democratic-NPL candidate for Attorney General, North Dakota · Challenger

Attorney, owner of Lamb Law Office in Grand Forks

Tim Lamb is a Grand Forks attorney and retired U.S. Army major. The North Dakota Democratic-NPL Party endorsed him for attorney general in March 2026, and he won the June 2026 Democratic primary. He was also the party's nominee for attorney general in 2022, when he lost to Drew Wrigley.

Where Lamb stands

Artificial intelligence regulation
Says AI needs government oversight and is concerned that AI models may become too powerful while President Trump and Congress are not seriously considering regulation. Says he would study what state AI legislation may be needed.
AI in law enforcement and the AG's office
Proposes assigning an assistant attorney general to become an expert on AI. Says AI will not replace human judgment in law. Called the Fargo-area facial recognition wrongful jailing a case where police were 'asleep at the wheel.'
Surveillance cameras (Flock)
Says Flock cameras should be limited to specific purposes, such as watching large crowds at football games or athletic venues, and not necessarily used for everyday activity on street corners.
Social media and child safety
Has said the attorney general's office should have done more to get North Dakota a larger share of the 47-state Meta child safety settlement.
Consumer protection
Says he would make consumer protection against AI fraud a priority and would work with other state attorneys general on AI oversight.

Background

  • U.S. Army, 20 years; retired as a major
  • J.D., University of North Dakota School of Law
  • Private-practice attorney since 2010; owns Lamb Law Office, Grand Forks
  • Democratic-NPL nominee for North Dakota Attorney General, 2022 (lost to Drew Wrigley, 28.8%)
  • Endorsed by the Democratic-NPL for State Auditor, 2024
  • Endorsed by the Democratic-NPL for Attorney General, March 2026; won the June 2026 Democratic primary
